text: Runs in expensive peak hours on the dishwasher-like channel (consistent pattern). Starting it after the peak hours would have saved about 8.7 SEK and 0.21 kgCO2e in 28 days with the same kWh, if you pay hourly spot prices. Action: start it after the evening peak (e.g. 21:00).
assumptions: F007-A04 treated as dishwasher-like (ASSUMPTION: channels are unlabelled)
counterfactual: runs moved to the first later non-peak hour (same kWh)
SEK = spot price only, excludes network fee, energy tax, VAT; depends on the student's tariff
frozen references (other flats, benchmarks, imputations) unchanged

text: Heater-like use while nobody is home on the heater-like channel (possible heating opportunity, needs confirmation). Over 28 observed days this was about 9.2 kWh and 5.7 SEK at spot prices (not extrapolated to a year). Action: check whether a portable heater is being used and ask your manager about radiators.
assumptions: F007-A07 treated as heater-like (ASSUMPTION: channels are unlabelled)
counterfactual: heater-like use removed only in hours with nobody home (absences >= 2 h)
SEK = spot price only, excludes network fee, energy tax, VAT; depends on the student's tariff
frozen references (other flats, benchmarks, imputations) unchanged
occupancy is a simulated sensor estimate; heating need on return (rebound) not modelled in the central case
